overall: The AG found the Somerset Board of Selectmen did not violate the Open Meeting Law in its October 25, 2023 executive session convening or minutes practices, and declined to review the general minutes-review allegation.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board could not have completed the executive session convening steps in the one minute between the 5:00 call to order and the 5:01 executive session on the notice.
allegations.key_passage: We find no evidence, and the complaint provides no support to the allegation, that the Board did not conduct all the procedural requirements prior to convening in executive session during the October 25, 2023, meeting.

allegations.summary: Complaint argued the posted 5:01 P.M. executive session time could not be honored given the procedures required before convening in executive session.
allegations.key_passage: The Law requires only that a meeting start on or after the time indicated on its posted notice.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board does not post its executive session minutes.
allegations.key_passage: The Open Meeting Law does not require that public bodies post their minutes to a website or that minutes be submitted to the Town Clerk, but merely that meeting minutes be made available within 10 days of a request.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board fails to periodically review its executive session minutes to decide whether they can be released.
